Iti therassa mahākaccāyanassa
Thus, of the Elder Mahākaccāyana,
Jambuvanavāsino peṭakopadese
The dweller in Jambu-vana, in the Piṭaka-Disclosure,
Tatiyabhūmi suttādhiṭṭhānaṃ nāma.
The third chapter called the ‘Thread's Standpoint’.
4. Suttavicayacatutthabhūmi
4. The Fourth Stage: Investigation of Threads
40. Tattha katamo suttavicayo?
40. Herein, what is Investigation of Threads?
Tattha kusalehi dhammehi akusalehi dhammehi pubbāparaso sādhukaṃ upaparikkhiyati.
Herein, one should thoroughly examine the unwholesome states and unwholesome states in terms of their consecutivity.
Kiṃnu kho idaṃ suttaṃ ārabhi … pe … tehi suttehi saha adhisannaṭṭhehi yujjati udāhu na yujjatīti?
‘How then, did he instigate this Thread… etc. …? Is it construable with those Threads that are fully agreed upon, or is it not so construable?’
Yathā bhagavā kilese ādimhi tattha deseti.
According as the Blessed One teaches defilement there in the beginning, it should be scrutinized as follows:
Kiṃ desitaṃ?
What is taught?
Tesaṃ kilesānaṃ pahānaṃ udāhu no desitanti upaparikkhitabbaṃ.
It should be scrutinized: ‘Is the abandoning of those defilements taught there [too] or is it not taught?’
Yadi na desitaṃ bhagavati tesaṃ kilesānaṃ pahānaṃ kusalā dhammā pariyesitabbā yattha te akusalā pahānaṃ gacchanti.

If it is not taught by the Blessed One, then the wholesome states [which bring about the] abandoning of those defilements must be sought in the [kind of divine life lived under the] Blessed One, where those unwholesome states come to [their] abandonment.
Sace samannehamāno na labhati.
If, in searching, one does not find [them].
Tattha akusalā dhammā apakaḍḍhitabbā vīmaṃsitabbā, saṃkilesabhāgiyasuttaṃ, yadi kilesā apakaḍḍhiyantā.
In that case, the unwholesome states must be reserved [and] inquired into [further, taking the type of Thread in this case to be] that Dealing with Corruption, if the defilements are being reserved.
Ye vā na denti tattha upaparikkhitabbā ariyamaggadhammā tāsu bhūmīsu kilesā pahānaṃ gacchanti, udāhu na gacchantīti.

If they do not give the construing, then the noble path qualities must be scrutinized as to whether those defilements come to abandonment in these planes—[namely those of Seeing and Keeping-in-Being]—or do they not?
Yattakā pana kilesā desitā.
However, a certain number of defilements may be taught.
Na tattakā ariyadhammā desitā.
Without any correspondingly equal number of noble ideas being taught.
Yattha kilesā pahānaṃ gacchanti, tattha ye kilesā ariyadhammānaṃ paṭipakkhena na yujjanti, te apakaḍḍhitabbā, sace apakaḍḍhiyantā yojanaṃ deti.
Wherever any defilements come to [their] abandonment, any defilements [so far] not construable as opposites of noble ideas there must be reserved; if, when reserved, they give the construction.
Tattha evaṃ vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.
Herein, it must be inquired into as follows.
Dve tīṇi vā taduttari vā kilesā ekena ariyamaggena pahānaṃ gacchantīti.
‘Do two or three or more defilements come to [their] abandonment by means of any single Path?’
Sace evaṃ vīmaṃsiyantā yojanaṃ deti, tattha upaparikkhitabbaṃ.
If, when thus inquired into, they give the construction, [then that Thread] must be scrutinized therein.
Paramparāya vā piṭakasampadānena vā suttassa attho ca nattho ca.
It must be inquired into according to the lineage of teaching or by the collection of scriptures, [regarding] the Thread's meaning and [the rest of the six terms for phrasing-sequence].
Yaṃ vā na sakkā suttaṃ niddisituṃ neva suttaṃ vicikicchitabbaṃ.
Or if it is not possible to demonstrate the Thread, [still] the Thread need not be the object of uncertainty.
Evaṃ yathā ādimhi kusalā dhammā honti.
Thus, just as in the beginning, there are wholesome states.
Ye kilesā te pahīneyyāti.
Whatever the defilements, they must be abandoned.
Te upaparikkhitabbā.
They must be scrutinized.
Puro vā kusalo paṭipakkhena vā puro desanā, anūnā anadhikā uggahetabbā.
Whether the wholesome comes first or whether the teaching is arrived at through its opposite's coming first, the teaching must be taken as having nothing lacking or superfluous.
Yathā paṭhamo uttilo yesamidāni kilesānaṃ ye ariyadhammā desitā ime kilesā imehi ariyadhammehi pahīyanti, udāhu nappahīyantīti vicinitabbā.
Just as in the first statement, now again any noble ideas taught for the abandoning of any defilements must be investigated as to whether they are abandoned by these particular noble ideas or not.
Yadi upaparikkhiyamānā yujjanti, gahetabbā.
If, when so scrutinized, they are construable, then they can be accepted.
Atha na yujjanti, ye kilesā apaṭipakkhā honti, te kilesā aparipakkhitabbā.
But if they are not construable, then any defilements that are not opposites must not be scrutinized.
Ye ca ariyadhammā paṭipakkhā honti, te ariyadhammā apakaḍḍhitabbā.
And any noble ideas that are opposites must be reserved.
Na hi ariyadhammā anāgāmikilesappahānaṃ gacchanti, nāpi ariyadhammā sabbakilesānaṃ pahānāya saṃvattanti.
For noble ideas do not arrive at the abandonment of future defilements, neither does any noble idea bring about the abandoning of all defilements.
Yathā kusalā mettā akusalo rāgo na tu kusalā mettāti kāretvā akusalassa rāgassa pahānāya sambhavati byāpādo mettāya pahānaṃ gacchati.

As for example, while loving-kindness is profitable and lust unprofitable, yet taking loving-kindness as profitable does not bring about the abandoning of lust; it is in fact ill will that comes to abandonment by means of loving-kindness.
Tasmā ubho kilesā upaparikkhitabbā.
Therefore both sorts of defilement have to be scrutinized.
Yo yo ca dhammo upadisiyati kusalo vā akusalo vā so apakaḍḍhitabbo.
And whatever idea is disclosed, whether profitable or unprofitable, must be reserved.
Sace te yujjanti apakaḍḍhiyamāno natthi upaparikkhitabbaṃ.
If these are construed when reserved, then there is nothing more to be scrutinized.
Dve vā kilesā ekena ariyadhammena pahīneyyāti dvīhi vā ariyadhammehi eko vā kileso pahīyatīti.
Either the two defilements may be abandonable by the one noble idea, or else either one of the two defilements may be abandonable by two noble ideas.
Atha vā evampi upaparikkhiyamānaṃ yujjati, tattha vīmaṃsitabbaṃ vā yathā yujjati tattha vīmaṃsitabbaṃ vā, yathā nanu sakkā suttaṃ niddisituṃ, na hi sutte vicikicchitabbaṃ.

Or alternatively, also when one, on being scrutinized, is construed, herein it must be inquired into how it is construed, or it must be inquired into why it is that the Thread cannot be demonstrated; for no Thread must remain an object of uncertainty.
Kileso maṃ ariyadhammesu desitesu ubhayato upaparikkhitabbaṃ.
When defilements are taught, they should be scrutinized in both ways.
Kira ye vā ime kilesā desitā ye ca ariyadhammā desitā gāthāya vā byākaraṇena vā, kiṃ nu kho ime kilesā imehi ariyadhammehi pahīyanti, udāhu nappahīyanti?
It seems that these defilements are taught in this verse or prose-exposition: How then, are these defilements abandoned by these noble ideas or are they not?
Ime vā ariyadhammā imesaṃ kilesānaṃ pahānāya saṃvattantīti.
Or conversely, do these noble ideas lead to the abandonment of these defilements?
Kiñcāpi kusalehi dhammehi akusalā dhammā pahānaṃ gacchanti.
Although unprofitable ideas do come to abandonment by means of profitable ideas.
Na tu sabbehi ariyadhammehi sabbākusalā pahānaṃ gacchanti.
Still not all unprofitable ideas come to abandonment by means of any noble ideas.
Yathā mettā kusalo akusalo ca rāgo na tu kusalā mettā akusalo rāgoti kāretvā mettāya rāgo pahānaṃ, byāpādo mettāya pahānaṃ gacchanti.

As for example, while loving-kindness is profitable and lust unprofitable, yet, taking loving-kindness as profitable and lust as unprofitable, lust does not come to abandonment by means of loving-kindness; it is in fact ill will that comes to abandonment by means of loving-kindness.
Evaṃ kilesoti kāretvā suttena pahānaṃ gacchati.
Consequently, defilement does not come to abandonment in a given Thread simply by taking it as ‘defilement’.
Na sutto dhammoti kāretvā sabbaṃ kilesassa pahānāya saṃvattati.
Nor, simply by taking a profitable idea in a given Thread, does that lead to the abandonment of all defilements.
Yaṃ tu suttassa ariyadhammo saṃkilesapaṭipakkho, so tena pahānaṃ gacchatīti.
In fact, it is only when a noble idea belonging to a particular Thread is a defilement's opposite that that defilement comes to be abandoned by means of that noble idea.
41. Tattha kusale desite sutte byākaraṇe vā saṃkilesā na yujjanti ariyadhammā vā, te mahāpadese niddisitabbāvayavena apakaḍḍhitabbā.

41. Herein, when the profitable taught in a particular verse or prose-exposition in the Thread and the corruptions do not construe—or the noble ideas do not construe—these should be reserved in accordance with the parts of the formula for scrutinizing demonstrable in the Principal Appeals to Authority.
Tattha kilesehi ca desitehi ariyadhammesu ca yadipi tena ariyadhammena te kilesā pahānaṃ gacchanti.
Herein, if, with the defilements taught and with that noble idea among the noble ideas, those defilements do come to abandonment.
Tatthapi uttari upaparikkhitabbaṃ.
Tatthapi uttari upaparikkhitabbaṃ.
Kena kāraṇena ete kilesā pajahitabbā, kena kāraṇena ariyadhammā desitāti?
In which Path-function are these defilements abandonable? In which Path-function are these noble ideas taught?
Yena yena vā ākārena ariyadhammā desitā, tena tena pakārena ayaṃ kileso ṭhito.
In whichever mood the noble ideas are taught, that is the aspect in which this defilement stands.
Atthi hi eko kileso, tena vā ariyadhammā na aññathā aññathā pahātabbo, yathā diṭṭhi rāgo avijjā ca dassanena pahātabbā.
For there is one defilement abandonable by only one noble idea, not in any other way: while view and lust are abandonable by Seeing, not so ignorance.
Sā ce evañca avijjā bhāvanāya bhūmi vā dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
And if ignorance or ideas belonging to the plane of Keeping-in-Being are abandonable in this way, it is precisely that ignorance which belongs to the further side fetters.
Sāyeva uddhaṃbhāgiyaṃ asaṅkhatadassanāya vimuttiyā animittena cetosamādhinā amanasikārena pahīyati.
That is abandoned through the kind of non-attention that is due to the deliverance's signless heart-concentration for the purpose of seeing the undetermined.
Evaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ upaparikkhitabbaṃ.
That is how the Thread should be scrutinized that it is with its meaning and with its phrasing.

Ye dassanena pahātabbā kilesā dassanākārena ariyadhammo desito, bhāvanāya pahātabbā bhāvanākārena ariyadhammo desito, patisevanā pahātabbā patisevanākārena ariyadhammo desito, evaṃ vinodanapahātabbā yāva satta āsavā kātabbā, yāvaññathā.

When defilements are of the kind abandonable by Seeing, then the noble idea is taught in the mood of Seeing; when of the kind abandonable by Keeping-in-Being, then the noble idea is taught in the mood of Keeping-in-Being; when of the kind abandonable by right use, then the noble idea is taught in the mood of right use; and so on from those abandonable by removal down to the seven kinds of taints, which can be quoted.
Aññathā hesa dhammo pahātabbo aññenākārena ariyadhammo desito, so ariyadhammo aññathā pariyesitabbo.
In so far as this defilement idea is abandonable in the various other stages, the noble idea will be appropriately taught in another mood, and so that noble idea must be sought otherwise.
Yadi ayaṃ dhammo pariyesato yo ca deseti yena yenākārena, so ariyadhammo pariyesitabbo, tenākārena kileso pahīyati.

If this defilement-idea gives the construing for one when one is seeking it, then in whichever mood that noble idea can be sought out, that is the mood in which the particular defilement is abandoned.
So tattha upaparikkhitabbo.
That must be scrutinized therein.
Atha na yujjati yadi hi tena suttena vihitaṃ suttaṃ vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.
Atha na yujjati yadi hi tena suttena vihitaṃ suttaṃ vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.
Yathā yujjati, tathā gahetabbaṃ.
Yathā yujjati, tathā gahetabbaṃ.

Yathā na yujjati, tathā na gahetabbaṃ, addhā etaṃ bhagavatā na bhāsitaṃ, āyasmatā vā duggahitaṃ, yathā mahāpadese niddisitabbaṃ, bhagavatā yathābhūtaṃ desitaṃ, yo ca dhammo desito kusalo ca akusalo ca tassa dhammassa paccayo pariyesitabbo.

If it is not construable, it cannot be accepted: (Certainly this was not spoken by the Blessed One, or it has been wrongly taken by the venerable one), which is demonstrable according to the Principal Appeals to Authority. What is taught by the Blessed One is according to how things are, and whatever idea the Blessed One instigates in order to teach, that idea's condition must be sought out.
Na hi paccayā vinā dhammo appaccayo uppajjati.
For no idea arises unconditioned, without a condition.
Tattha ko ākāro pariyesanāya?
Herein, what is the mood for the search?
Tattha tathārūpaṃ sahetu sappaccayaṃ soyaṃ dhammo vuttoti idaṃ vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.
Herein, this Thread must be inquired into as to whether this idea in question has been stated with the cause and with the condition appropriate thereto.
So ca paccayo tividho – mudu majjho adhimatto.
And the condition is of three kinds: slight, medium, and outstanding.
Tattha mudumhi paccaye mududhammo gahetabbo, evaṃ satyesa paccayo duvidho paraṃparāpaccayo ca samanantarapaccayo ca.

Herein, when the condition is slight, the idea conditioned must be taken as slight. That being so, this condition is again of two kinds: condition in remote relation and condition in immediate proximity.
So paccayo mudutena byādhimattaṃ pariyesitabbaṃ.
When the condition is slight, what is unoutstanding owing to it must be sought.
Kiṃ kāraṇaṃ?
What is the reason?
Aññataropi paccayo aññehi paccayehi pariyattiṃ vā pāripūriṃ vā gacchati.
A certain condition comes to occurrence or fulfilment through other conditions.
Tattha yo dhammo desito, tassa dhammassa etena vā kāraṇena vā hetu pariyesitabbo.
Herein, whatever the idea taught in this Thread that is being scrutinized, the cause of that must be sought.
Yathā paccayo hetunā paccayena ca, so tassa dhammassa nissando pariyesitabbo.
And like the condition, the outcome of that idea must be sought by cause and by condition.
Yathā niddiṭṭho adhiṭṭhāne padhānaṃ pariyesati, so paccayo pariyesitabbo.
That condition should be sought in the way that one seeks how the basic state was demonstrated in the terms of expression of the particular Thread.
Na hi mudussa dhammassa adhimatto nissando adhimattassa vā nissandassa mududhammo, atha mudussa mudu majjhāya majjho adhimattassa adhimatto yujjati, taṃ gahetabbaṃ, atha na yujjati na gahetabbaṃ.

For there is no slight idea that has an outstanding outcome, nor does any outstanding outcome have a slight condition-idea. If the slight is construable of the slight, the medium of the medium, and the outstanding of the outstanding, that can be accepted. But if it does not so construe, it cannot be accepted.
Yañca bhagavā ārabhati dhammaṃ desetuṃ, taṃyeva dhammaṃ majjhantapariyosānaṃ deseti, yathā suttādhiṭṭhāne dhammā ādimhi niddisati, taṃyeva bahu tassa suttassa pariyosānaṃ.

And whatever idea the Blessed One instigates initially in order to teach a particular teaching, that he teaches also in the middle and the end of it: he demonstrates in the beginning the idea according as it is given in the terms of expression of that particular teaching, and only that idea appears much in it and is that Thread's end.
Tassa hi dhammassa vasena taṃ suttaṃ hoti gāthā vā byākaraṇaṃ khuddakaṃ mahantaṃ vā, yathā pana duvidhā anurūpanti vā thapanā ca desanāthapanā.

For it is in virtue of that idea that that Thread comes to be such as it is in type, whether verse or prose-exposition, whether small or large; but as the fixing is twofold, namely fixing that is in conformity as well as fixing the actual teaching, the fixing of that idea must also be sought as to whether it is in conformity with other Threads.
Rūpantipi dhammassa pariyesitabbā.
Rūpantipi dhammassa pariyesitabbā.
Yathā ca bhagavatā pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ saṃvaraṇaṃ desitaṃ taṇhāya niggahaṇatthaṃ icchāva hoti.
Just as the restraining of the five faculties taught by the Blessed One, in having for its purpose the curbing of craving, teaches that that idea conveys his wish.
Deseti yathā gopālakopame sutte aññehipi suttehi bhagavā bhāsati icchāva hoti majjhimanikāye vitakko ayaṃ bhagavato desanānurūpanti iti so dhammo aññesupi veyyākaraṇesu pariyesitabbo.

As in the simile of the Cattle-herd Thread, when tested also by means of other Threads that the Blessed One has uttered, the thought in the Majjhima Nikāya conveys his wish. This is what is in conformity with the Blessed One's teaching. So this idea has to be sought also in other prose-expositions; for it cannot be regarded as sought out in only a single Thread.
Na hi ekaṃ hi sutte daṭṭhabbo.
Na hi ekaṃ hi sutte daṭṭhabbo.
Yujjanaṃ taṃ gahetabbaṃ.
When it construes, it can be accepted.
42. Tattha katamaṃ anuññātaṃ?
42. Herein, what is the agreed?
Yaṃ kiñci suttaṃ bhagavatā na bhāsitaṃ tañca suttesuyeva ndissati, evametaṃ dhāretabbaṃ.
When any Thread whatever is not uttered by the Blessed One and that Thread is found among the Threads too, then according as it is uttered by whomsoever it may be, so it should be borne in mind.
Yathā asukena bhāsitanti, taṃ suttaṃ vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.
That Thread must be inquired into as follows.
Kiṃ nu kho imaṃ suttaṃ anuññātaṃ khamaṃ bhagavato udāhu nānuññātaṃ khamaṃ, kiñci rūpañca suttaṃ bhagavato anuññātaṃ khamaṃ kiñci rūpañca nānuññātaṃ khamaṃ?
‘How then, does this Thread allow of the Blessed One's agreement or does it not allow of his agreement?’
Yaṃ sabbaso anotāretvā dasabalo gocaraṃ deseti, taṃ sabbaṃ suttaṃ bhagavato nānuññātaṃ khamaṃ.
When someone teaches what is the Ten Powered One's province, altogether without giving a way of entry, that Thread does not allow of the Blessed One's agreement.

Atthipi so sāvako dasabalānaṃ gocaraṃ jānāti odhiso anodhiso, taṃ pana balaṃ sabbaso na jānāti aññathā nāma savanena, yathā āyasmatā sāriputtena yena brāhmaṇo ovadito, tassa āyasmato natthi indriyabalavemattañāṇaṃ, tena puggalaparo [puggalo paroparañca (pī.)] parañca taṃ ajānanto sati uttarikaraṇīye uppādito, so bhagavatā apasādito.

But there is also the kind of hearer who knows the Ten Powered One's province, yet he does not know that power itself at all beyond the hearing of it; as in the case of the divine exhorted by the venerable Sāriputta. Now that venerable one had no Knowledge of Variety in Faculties and Powers, hence by his not knowing the Encompassing of Other Persons, he was made to reappear after death, and so the venerable Sāriputta was not congratulated by the Blessed One.

Yathāva āyasmā mahākassapo bhāgineyyaṃ ovadati anantariyasamannāgato iddhipāṭihīrena aṅguliyo adīpetvā yaṃ sabbesaṃ dhammānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ hetuso ṭhānaso yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ, tassa āyasmato saṃvijjate, tena naṃ ovadati, taṃ bhagavā karoti.

And as in the case of the venerable Mahā-Kassapa when he advised his nephew, since no knowledge of how things are by cause and instance in the case of all Undertaking of Action existed in that venerable one, hence the Blessed One advised him.
‘‘ Sacepi dasa pajjote, dhārayissasi kassapa;
‘Even, O Kassapa, if thou wilt carry ten such luminaries,’
Neva dakkhati rūpāni, cakkhu tassa na vijjatī ’’ ti.
‘Not even then will he see forms: That eye does not exist in him.’
